datePolicy.deletionRule: Do not delete historical events during refresh. Do not remove future events only because they disappeared from a listing page.
datePolicy.cancelRule: Mark an event cancelled only when the official source explicitly says it is cancelled.

eligibilityPolicy.defaultRule: Keep events that children can reasonably attend or that are family-compatible, even when the event is not exclusively for children.
eligibilityPolicy.grayAreaRule: Keep gray-area community events unless the event is clearly adult-only, unsafe, or inappropriate for children.
grayAreaExamplesToKeep: community health or safety events with family participation
excludeSignals: beer garden as the primary activity
explicitly unsafe or inappropriate for children
eligibilityPolicy.exclusionRule: Exclude only when children clearly cannot attend or the event is clearly not suitable for children.

eventSchemaGuidance.summaryRule: Summary should contain activity content only. Do not put date, time, venue, room, place, or address text in summary.
eventSchemaGuidance.sourceUrlRule: Keep the original official event page when available. If only a calendar listing exists, keep that listing URL.
eventSchemaGuidance.evidenceRule: Manual or configured events should keep evidenceUrl, evidenceType, and checkedAt when practical.

eventStatuses.review: Event is useful but has incomplete or uncertain fields.
eventStatuses.cancelled: Official source explicitly says the event is cancelled.
eventStatuses.stale_possible: Future event was previously seen but no longer appears on the source; not enough evidence to cancel.
eventStatuses.duplicate: Event was merged into a better canonical record.

confidenceGuidance.meaning: Official API or structured official detail page with complete fields.
Official page with some inferred or cleaned fields.
Official flyer, manual transcription, or configured source with enough evidence.
Third-party directory or incomplete source; keep only if useful and mark for review.

qualityChecks: Every real event should have a stable id and sourceId.
Every real event should have a sourceUrl or url back to the source.
Every displayed map event should have coordinates or a geocodable address.
Do not invent activity descriptions when the source does not provide one.
Prefer official HTML text before image, flyer, or OCR text.
Use image or flyer text only when normal page text is missing needed date, time, room, address, or venue detail.
